title: An experiment that measures two things at once
promptMarkdown: For the A ⇌ B system of problem1, propose a small numerical or paper experiment at C=0.250M using starts B₀=0 and B₀=0.250M, with observations t=0,20,60,120min. Calculate both predicted time courses. A catalyst doubles k_f and k_r. Which quantities change, which stay fixed, and how would you estimate both the equilibrium fraction and relaxation rate from noisy measurements without assuming that the final observed sample is exactly equilibrium? Give a conservation check and one model-failure criterion.
hintLadder: Use the solution B=Beq+(B0−Beq)e^(−λt) for each start.
A catalyst scaling both rates changes λ only.
Jointly fit the endpoint instead of declaring the last sample exact.

criteria.criterion: Calculates both trajectories and catalyst effect
